podcast.body: This song was mentioned as one of the popular tracks in 1973, following the number one song "Tie a Yellow Ribbon around the Old Oak Tree." This era of "safe and bland" music on AM radio contributed to the desire for a "reboot" that punk rock eventually provided. "I was followed by Jim Crochet and Bad Bad Lee Roy Brown."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: This song was the winner of the 1973 Billboard Song of the Summer. It is described as "goofy, slap happy, and sturdy" and was notable for being the only song of the summer from the first half of the 70s that was not a ballad, giving it a distinct advantage with its tempo. "It's The Goofy, Slap Happy, and Strudy, Bad, Bad, Lee Roy Brown."
